heading: Weight decay favors efficient generalizing circuits over memorization
definition: weight decay (or another bias toward low norm) favours a more efficient generalizing circuit over memorization, which predicts a critical dataset size and "ungrokking" below it.
summary: Small algorithmic experiments link circuit efficiency (generalizing with smaller weights) to a threshold dataset size and to loss of generalization after reducing data. Independent groups reproduce regularization’s contribution to generalization, but the full explanation that weight decay favors efficient generalizing circuits over memorization has not been independently reproduced.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/small algorithmic settings: R0 for the joint measured-efficiency and reduced-data-ungrokking account; R2 for the narrower regularization/generalization component. <1B: ? for the complete account. 1-10B: ? for the complete account; a narrower decay ablation exists. 10-100B and >100B: no V5 coverage recorded.
suggested_status.reason: arXiv:2309.02390#r7, arXiv:2309.02390#r8 and arXiv:2309.02390#r9 combine measured relative efficiency with reduced-data ungrokking. arXiv:2509.21519#R8 and arXiv:2509.21519#R9 supply related sample-size and representation-efficiency theory but leave ungrokking untested. arXiv:2407.20199#R25, arXiv:2407.20199#R26 and arXiv:2407.20199#R27 reproduce the narrower regularization contribution in quadratic networks. The checker assigns that study T2: its principal AGOP-based kernel-RFM test uses a different method, while its neural-network comparison reproduces prior fully connected experiments. arXiv:2310.06110#R12 and arXiv:2310.06110#R13 show grokking with increasing total norm and zero explicit decay; relative circuit efficiency is unmeasured, so these receive no V5 verdict. Its decay/output-scale sweep likewise supplies no V5 limitation. Component reproduction does not establish independent reproduction of the full chain. counts: versions.V5.verdicts and versions.V5.tested_by_tranche retain pre-check classifications; versions.V5.studies_by_size and versions.V5.coverage_by_operation show limited explicitly sized coverage and no buckets above 10B.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent test jointly measuring competing-circuit efficiency, predicting the data boundary and demonstrating reduced-data ungrokking would change the full-account level. Matched tests should distinguish norm geometry from output-scale mediation and repeat the chain with alternative regularizers and realistic pretrained models.

source.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
source.authors: Neel Nanda; Lawrence Chan; Tom Lieberum; J. Smith; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: The study varied training data and weight decay in one-layer transformers learning modular addition.
original_result.result: The study argued that weight decay favors a Fourier circuit with smaller weights over memorization, while squared weight norm fell as the circuit formed and memorizing components were removed. With modulus 113, 10% or 20% training data produced no grokking after 40k epochs, whereas 30–50% did.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

wording_issues.phrase: weight decay (or another bias toward low norm)
wording_issues.issue: Specify the regularized quantity. Parameter L1, L2, L∞ and nuclear norms, activation norms and function-Jacobian norms are distinct. Successful L1-regularized generalization can accompany increasing L2 norm; that measurement alone cannot determine relative circuit efficiency. MAN regularizes E[||a||_2], without squaring the activation norm, and achieves generalization.

The direction is conditional. In Gaussian linear classification with γ=25 and n=32, late low-norm bias destroys generalization: test accuracy falls from 100% to nearly 50%, directly challenging an unrestricted favorable preference. Effective decay can lengthen or prevent target attainment. At decay λ=2.0, the counting transformer underfits and fails to learn the task; this is failure of the generalizing solution to emerge.

Specify the efficiency measure: fixed-logit parameter norm and theoretical hidden-node counts measure different quantities. Extracted core dimensionality is also distinct from norm efficiency. Post-grokking core expansion and additional rotational modes under continued decay are compatible with minimum-norm redundancy; they do not test competition with memorization or contradict greater norm efficiency. Better fixed-norm performance does not uniquely predict representation choice.

Specify the training protocol associated with the boundary. Width-dependent thresholds support a conditional critical-size prediction; V5 does not assert a model-independent threshold. Knowledge distillation with Adam enables generalization at 20% training data where scratch training fails after 30,000 iterations. This reverses an unconditional below-threshold failure reading, without measuring relative circuit efficiency. Composition behavior can remain unchanged as dataset size varies at fixed fact ratio.

Reserve this prediction for losing generalization after retraining an already generalized model on reduced data. Scratch-training failure, semi-grokking, model-size sweeps called ungrokking and late collapse without dataset reduction test different outcomes.

Separate measurements of decay dependence, total norm and dataset thresholds do not establish the causal chain. Toy effective theory predicts representation rate λ3=0 with high probability below a training fraction of approximately 0.4 and increasing average λ3 above it; low-norm circuit selection and ungrokking are not demonstrated. Reduced-landscape estimates likewise need their theoretical scope stated. Alternative threshold derivations and deviations from an inverse-decay timing approximation do not establish failure of V5's preference. Modular-addition MLP interventions also show substantial mediation of norm effects by logit scale.

V5 does not require total norm to decrease from initialization or explicit weight decay to be present. Zero-decay modular-arithmetic and polynomial-regression MLPs, and MNIST norm-increasing interventions, exhibit grokking with increasing norms. These trajectories do not measure relative memorizing/generalizing circuit efficiency or exclude an implicit low-norm bias; they cannot determine whether V5's preference holds.

Optimizer and parameterization matter: weight-decay timing trends differ across AdamW, Muon and Adam, but that comparison does not isolate decay implementation. Radial L2 and spectral low-rank decay differ in scale-invariant layers.

method_sensitivity.what: Weak decay can preserve memorization, moderate decay enables or accelerates generalization, and excessive decay can impair learning. In 10.18653/v1/2026.findings-acl.1301, λ=2.0 causes underfitting and failure to learn; numerical accuracy is unstated. In arXiv:2605.20441's canonical transformer, λ=10 produces identical attention patterns and absent generalization; failure to fit training data is not reported. The MNIST MLP inverse-decay timing relation holds approximately over 0.1–1; deviations outside this interval qualify that timing approximation, without testing V5's circuit-efficiency or critical-size predictions. The informal modular-addition discussion in lw:BYwGEBspGgPY5nBZN reports explicit regularization helping some architectures, harming some frozen-layer settings, and almost never being necessary except in edge cases; architectures are incompletely specified, and efficiency and norm bias are unmeasured.

method_sensitivity.factor: Optimizer, learning rate and attention decay
method_sensitivity.what: Full-batch GD and WanD permit generalization without explicit decay; these observations do not determine whether an implicit low-norm bias selects a more efficient generalizing circuit. Regularization and adaptive optimizers generally reduce grokking time in arXiv:2301.02679, without measuring circuit efficiency. Stronger-decay acceleration is clear for AdamW and Muon but not evident for Adam in arXiv:2605.18022's tested sweeps; coupled L2 implementation is not established. Matching attention decay changes the Muon comparison in arXiv:2606.29176.

method_sensitivity.factor: Norm definition, regularizer geometry and targeted matrix
method_sensitivity.what: L1, nuclear and Jacobian penalties act on different quantities. In arXiv:2506.05718, d1=d2=2^6=64; successful L1-regularized generalization accompanies increasing parameter L2 norm, which alone cannot determine relative circuit efficiency. In arXiv:2610.35112's MLP, a W1 nuclear penalty delays onset despite compression, while all penalized runs still generalize. Its transformer rank-cap comparisons change capacity and grokking reliability rather than isolate a low-norm bias. Neither result establishes reversal or failure of V5's efficiency preference. In scale-invariant layers, low-rank decay differs from radial L2 decay.

Temperature substantially mediates norm-induced delay under cross-entropy, changing timing while raised norm stays fixed; MSE shows a smaller norm effect through an uncharacterized route. These qualify a scalar-norm timing explanation without establishing failure of endpoint circuit selection. In arXiv:2310.06110's one-layer transformer, stronger decay removes delay at fixed laziness α, and raising α restores it; relative circuit efficiency is unmeasured. Compositional comparisons in arXiv:2405.05409 change initialization and decay jointly, preventing attribution to decay alone or identification of V5's mechanism. The arXiv:2501.08537 endpoint comparisons likewise do not measure reduced-data ungrokking.

method_sensitivity.factor: Architecture, normalization, projection and structural priors
method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:2507.20057, periodic parameter projection permits rapid generalization at approximately fixed norm without layer normalization; with layer normalization, scale decay restores generalization. This qualifies explanations requiring norm reduction; circuit efficiency remains unmeasured. Hidden-vector projection with normalized readout in arXiv:2611.03156 differs from parameter decay; decay-free crossings do not establish a V5 limitation. In arXiv:2603.05228's fully bounded spherical transformer on Z113 addition (30% training), mean generalization epoch at learning rate 6e-4 is 820 without decay versus 1,560 with decay 1, without a separable memorization phase. With uniform attention, zero decay gives concurrent generalization, whereas decay destabilizes and delays it, with 6/10 successful seeds. Parameter-norm trajectories are unreported; another efficiency bias remains untested. In arXiv:2607.12735's modular addition, structural priors weaken clamped-norm timing sensitivity; this algorithmic-only result does not establish V3's non-algorithmic-data component.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data information, distribution, width and initialization history
method_sensitivity.what: Thresholds shift with width and with random versus already-generalized initialization; width dependence is compatible with V5's critical-size prediction. Teacher-provided soft labels cross a label-only scratch boundary: in arXiv:2511.04760, distillation with Adam enables generalization at a 20% training fraction, whereas scratch training fails after 30,000 iterations. This reverses unconditional below-threshold failure under changed training information, without measuring relative circuit efficiency. Composition behavior depends on inferred/atomic fact ratio and is qualitatively unchanged by size at fixed ratio.

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention timing and acquisition versus retention
method_sensitivity.what: Early-plateau decay pulses lack stable dose ordering, whereas middle-to-late pulses produce ordered timing shifts relative to an unperturbed baseline. The cohort comparison uses normalized training phase; absolute epoch boundaries belong to an illustrated run. Temporary interventions at a geometric flag alter onset. Maintaining decay after grokking can expand extracted cores and rotational modes; this is compatible with the paper's minimum-norm explanation and does not measure competition with memorization. Fixed-decay ordinal models can later lose structured generalization, but temporal degradation does not test critical-size-induced ungrokking or a V5 guarantee of permanent retention.

Finite-budget non-grokking does not establish permanent failure. The escape-time rows in arXiv:2605.24057 provide horizon-dependent behavioral coverage, without testing V5's efficiency mechanism. Time from training start differs from the post-memorization gap: arXiv:2605.20441's time-to-grok measure lacks training-saturation timing. Crossing 99% differs from sustaining it or finishing near-perfect; the fixed-512 modular-division result in 10.3389/frai.2026.1860893 crosses the threshold but later has lower final accuracy, without testing a V5 stability prediction. Under a fixed budget, decay's favorable effect on incidence becomes stronger with model scale in arXiv:2609.20166; the smaller favorable effect at 12K also supports the narrower decay–generalization association.

Fixed orderings reduce epochs to finish relative to fresh random permutations, and their relative advantage increases as decay weakens. A decay sweep therefore depends on ordering even with the task and training set fixed.

method_sensitivity.factor: Seed variability, censoring and evidence form
method_sensitivity.what: Circuit-efficiency measurements have substantial seed variability; an illustrative semi-grokking trajectory is cherry-picked, transient, and eventually reaches full generalization. Its transient plateau confirms V5's semi-grokking prediction rather than demonstrating partial failure. High-norm clamp results in algorithmic modular addition are censored, so the reported slowdown is a lower bound; they establish norm-dependent timing without testing non-algorithmic coverage. Dynamic-decay improvements have mixed statistical evidence. The norm–onset association in arXiv:2609.10657 is indeterminate because prose and figure statistics conflict; its MLP architecture and scaling analysis constitute a different method from the original transformer.
